what_happened.line: The Select Board announced, on returning from executive session, that it had voted to accept a three-year police union contract; the vote count was not stated.
The town manager said year one of the contract is covered by the existing appropriation because of attrition, so no new money is needed for it.
The Town Meeting article for the police contract will be passed over because year one needs no appropriation.
The contract changes longevity pay from a percentage-based system to a flat dollar amount, and corrects the gap between patrol officer steps.
The board adjourned, noting next Tuesday's special Town Meeting.

why_it_matters: The contract sets police pay for three years, and years two and three will need to be paid for in later budgets, so it bears on future tax bills even though year one needs no new appropriation.
Because the article is being passed over, voters at the special Town Meeting will not be asked to vote on money for this contract.
watch_next: The special Town Meeting next Tuesday, where the police contract article is expected to be passed over.
The budgets for years two and three of the contract, when its later-year costs will need funding.
